title_en: Suixi County Dumiao Timber Market Co., Ltd. v. Cong Jiagen — dispute over removal of nuisance
ruling_gist_en: The content of a final judgment serving as the basis for enforcement shall be clear and specific. If a final judgment cannot be enforced and indeed contains errors, the issue should not be resolved through another lawsuit procedure, but rather through the trial supervision procedure.

full_text_en:
Suixi County Dumiao Timber Large Market Co., Ltd. v. Cong Jiagen — Dispute over Nuisance Removal

Ruling Summary

The content of an effective judgment serving as a basis for enforcement shall be clear and specific. If an effective judgment cannot be enforced and is indeed erroneous, it should not be resolved through a separate lawsuit procedure, but rather through a trial supervision procedure.

Plaintiff: Suixi County Dumiao Timber Large Market Co., Ltd., domiciled in Suixi County, Anhui Province.
Legal Representative: Zhang Shouwei, Manager of the Company.

Defendant: Cong Jiagen, male, 46 years old, residing in Suixi County, Anhui Province.

Plaintiff Suixi County Dumiao Timber Large Market Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dumiao Timber Market) filed a lawsuit with the Suixi County People's Court of Anhui Province due to a dispute over nuisance removal with Defendant Cong Jiagen.

Plaintiff Dumiao Timber Market alleged: In 2011, Defendant Cong Jiagen rented 2.6 mu (approximately 0.173 hectares) of land from Dumiao Timber Market and built four temporary structures within the rented area. After the contract expired, Cong Jiagen refused to perform the renewal obligation and also refused to vacate. For this reason, Dumiao Timber Market filed a lawsuit with the Suixi County People's Court of Anhui Province, requesting a judgment ordering Cong Jiagen to return the land use right and compensate for losses. The court upheld the claims of Dumiao Timber Market. Cong Jiagen, dissatisfied with the judgment, filed an appeal. The Huaibei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province dismissed Cong Jiagen's appeal and upheld the first-instance judgment. Dumiao Timber Market then applied to the Suixi County People's Court of Anhui Province for compulsory enforcement. During the enforcement period of that court, Cong Jiagen actually compensated Dumiao Timber Market for losses up to the end of 2014. However, during enforcement, Cong Jiagen still refused to demolish the buildings and piled objects within the land use right scope of Dumiao Timber Market. Accordingly, [the plaintiff] requests a judgment ordering Cong Jiagen to remove the nuisance, demolish all buildings and piled objects within his 2.6 mu land use right scope, and compensate Dumiao Timber Market for losses from January 1, 2015, with specific standards referring to the judgment (2014) Sui Min Er Chu Zi No. 0010.

Defendant Cong Jiagen argued: Plaintiff Dumiao Timber Market did not legally obtain the right to use the land in dispute, and its lawsuit itself lacks standing. The adjudicative results of the two previously effective judgments concerning the case lack factual and legal basis and cannot serve as the basis for deciding this case. Moreover, Cong Jiagen has new evidence sufficient to refute the above two judgments. The agreement signed on October 1, 2008 between Dumiao Timber Market and the involved villagers is a void agreement. The agreement signed between Dumiao Timber Market and Cong Jiagen is likewise a void agreement, and neither is protected by law. The land that Cong Jiagen currently operates is based on an agreement signed on September 5, 2013 with the relevant villagers, and has no relation to Dumiao Timber Market. In summary, Dumiao Timber Market has no legal relationship with this case, and [the defendant] requests that its claims be dismissed.

The Suixi County People's Court of Anhui Province found the following facts at first instance:

On October 1, 2008, Zhang Shouwei, Legal Representative of Plaintiff Dumiao Timber Market, signed a "Land Lease Agreement" in the name of Huaibei Building Materials Market (which had not been legally registered) with 32 farming households of Wangtielu Villagers Group, Dumiao Village, Suixi Town, Suixi County. The villagers voluntarily leased a total of 75.79 mu of their contracted land to Huaibei Building Materials Market for the construction of a panel market. The lease term was from October 1, 2008 to October 1, 2018.

On June 20, 2011, Dumiao Timber Market was legally registered and established, with Legal Representative being Zhang Shouwei.

On July 1, 2011, Dumiao Timber Market and Defendant Cong Jiagen signed a "Site Lease Agreement", which stipulated that Dumiao Timber Market would lease 2.6 mu of land to Cong Jiagen for use, with annual rent of 3,446 yuan per mu, and a usage term ending on July 1, 2013.

After the lease expired, Cong Jiagen neither renewed nor vacated, and Dumiao Timber Market thus filed a lawsuit with the Suixi County People's Court of Anhui Province, requesting Cong Jiagen to return the use right of the 2.6 mu land and compensate for losses of 100,000 yuan. The Suixi County People's Court of Anhui Province rendered Civil Judgment (2014) Sui Min Er Chu Zi No. 00010 on June 17, 2014: 1. Cong Jiagen shall, within five days after the judgment takes effect, return to Dumiao Timber Market the use right of 2.6 mu of land (the land location: adjacent to Zhao Depeng and Wang Shaoqing on the north, Xu Jun on the west, the roadside on the south, and the river embankment base on the east; i.e., taking a point from the center of the south road, measuring 35.5 meters wide vertically northward, then 48.6 meters long vertically eastward, forming a rectangular area), and compensate Dumiao Timber Market for economic losses of 8,586.3 yuan (3,446 ÷ 12 × 11.5 × 2.6); losses after June 20, 2014 shall continue to be calculated according to this standard until the date of performance of the limited debt; 2. Dismiss the other claims of Dumiao Timber Market.

Cong Jiagen, dissatisfied, appealed to the Huaibei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province, which rendered Civil Judgment (2014) Huai Min Er Zhong Zi No. 00160 on September 24, 2014, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

During the period when Dumiao Timber Market applied to the original trial court for enforcement, Cong Jiagen had actually compensated Dumiao Timber Market for losses before December 31, 2014. The buildings and piled objects on the 2.6 mu of land have not been demolished to date.

The Suixi County People's Court of Anhui Province held at first instance:

A citizen who breaches a contract shall bear civil liability. In this case, Defendant Cong Jiagen leased 2.6 mu of land from Plaintiff Dumiao Timber Market. After the contract expired, his continued possession and use of the leased property lacked legal basis, and he should, by law, return it. The buildings and piled objects on the involved land should be demolished. Therefore, the court supports Plaintiff Dumiao Timber Market's claim requiring Cong Jiagen to demolish the buildings and piled objects on the involved land. The infringed party has the right to request the infringer to bear tort liability, and the losses caused by the infringer shall be compensated. Cong Jiagen's continued possession and use of the leased property after the contract expired without legal basis caused certain economic losses to the plaintiff. He should compensate Dumiao Timber Market for losses according to the contemporaneous land lease fee, at the standard of annual rent of 3,446 yuan per mu from January 2015.

In summary, in accordance with Article 106, paragraph 1, and Article 134 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, Articles 8, 44, and 235 of the Contract Law of the PRC, Articles 3 and 15 of the Tort Liability Law of the PRC, Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, the Suixi County People's Court of Anhui Province rendered the following judgment on April 27, 2015:

1. Defendant Cong Jiagen shall, within five days from the date this judgment takes effect, demolish the buildings and other piled objects within the scope of the 2.6 mu land use right of Plaintiff Suixi County Dumiao Timber Large Market Co., Ltd. (the land location: adjacent to Zhao Depeng and Wang Shaoqing on the north, Xu Jun on the west, the roadside on the south, and the river embankment base on the east; i.e., taking a point from the center of the south road, measuring 35.5 meters wide vertically northward, then 48.6 meters long vertically eastward, forming a rectangular area);

2. Defendant Cong Jiagen shall compensate Plaintiff Suixi County Dumiao Timber Large Market Co., Ltd. for economic losses according to the standard of (3,446 ÷ 12 × 2.6), calculated from January 1, 2015 until the date when Cong Jiagen demolishes the buildings and other piled objects within the 2.6 mu land use right scope of Suixi County Dumiao Timber Large Market Co., Ltd.

Cong Jiagen, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Huaibei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province, arguing:

The appellee Dumiao Timber Market was registered and established on June 20, 2011, and has no legal relationship with the disputed land and the attachments thereon. The "Land Lease Agreement" signed on October 1, 2008 by Zhang Shouwei in the name of Huaibei Building Materials Market with 32 farming households of Wangtielu Villagers Group, Dumiao Village, Suixi Town, Suixi County, and the "Site Lease Agreement" signed on July 1, 2011 between Dumiao Timber Market and Cong Jiagen both violate mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, are not legally binding on the parties, and are void agreements. The two-instance civil judgments in the previous case erred in fact-finding and application of law, and cannot serve as the basis for deciding the case. Cong Jiagen signed a "Land Lease Agreement" on September 5, 2013 with 32 farming households of Wangtielu Villagers Group, Dumiao Village, Suixi Town, Suixi County, and paid rent in accordance with the agreement. Cong Jiagen's operation and use of the land in dispute has no legal connection with Dumiao Timber Market, and Dumiao Timber Market's claims for nuisance removal and compensation for losses lack factual and legal basis. Request the second instance to revoke the original judgment and dismiss Dumiao Timber Market's claims.

The appellee Dumiao Timber Market argued in the second instance: The facts involved in the appeal of Appellant Cong Jiagen have already been determined by the two-instance civil judgments in the previous case, and the judgments have not been revoked. Cong Jiagen's grounds of appeal are untenable, and the appeal should be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

The Huaibei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province, upon second instance, confirmed the facts found in the first instance. Additionally, it found: The "Site Lease Agreement" signed between appellee Dumiao Timber Market and appellant Cong Jiagen had a lease term from October 1, 2008 to July 1, 2013. Cong Jiagen separately signed a "Land Lease Agreement" with 32 farming households of Wangtielu Villagers Group, Dumiao Village, Suixi Town, Suixi County on September 5, 2013 regarding the land in dispute.

The Huaibei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province held in the second instance:

After the lease contract signed between appellee Dumiao Timber Market and appellant Cong Jiagen expired, because Cong Jiagen did not return the leased land, [Dumiao Timber Market] filed a lawsuit requesting Cong Jiagen to return the land use right and compensate for losses. The dispute between the parties has been confirmed by this court's Civil Judgment (2014) Huai Min Er Zhong Zi No. 00160. Dumiao Timber Market has already applied for enforcement to the first-instance court in that case. The present judgment and the previous judgment are based on the same facts and reasons, constituting a duplicative lawsuit. The original trial court's judgment on the same dispute again was improper and should be corrected. Further analysis is as follows:

According to Article 124, item 5 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, "In cases where a judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement has already taken legal effect, if a party files another lawsuit, the plaintiff shall be informed to apply for retrial, except for rulings where the people's court has permitted withdrawal of the lawsuit." This is generally considered the basic expression of the principle of res judicata in China's civil procedure law. Article 247 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, effective from February 4, 2015, provides: "Where a party files a lawsuit again regarding a matter already initiated during the litigation process or after the judgment takes effect, and the following conditions are simultaneously met, it constitutes a duplicative lawsuit: (1) the parties in the subsequent lawsuit and the previous lawsuit are the same; (2) the subject matter of the subsequent lawsuit and the previous lawsuit is the same; (3) the claims in the subsequent lawsuit are the same as those in the previous lawsuit, or the claims in the subsequent lawsuit substantially negate the adjudicative result of the previous lawsuit." "If a party files a duplicative lawsuit, a ruling shall be made not to accept the case; if already accepted, a ruling shall be made to dismiss the case, unless otherwise provided by law or judicial interpretation."

Regarding the land lease contract dispute between the parties, before this case, the second instance court had already rendered an effective judgment. In that case, the claims of appellee Dumiao Timber Market were to request an order for appellant Cong Jiagen to return the land use right and compensate for losses before return. During the enforcement period after Dumiao Timber Market won the case, the first instance court only actually enforced the compensation for losses part up to December 31, 2014, but because there were buildings and piled objects constructed by Cong Jiagen on the land, it was unable to actually enforce the "return" of the land in dispute. The question now is: what is the relationship between the claim for "nuisance removal" in this case and the claims in the previous case? Logically, if the "nuisance removal" cannot be effectively carried out regarding the attachments on the land, then the previous judgment on "return of land use right" would only be empty and become a piece of paper that is difficult to enforce and cannot be implemented. The claim for compensation for losses from January 1, 2015 in this case, from a literal understanding, must be part of the previous judgment's compensation for losses from 2013. In other words, these two claims in this case are inseparable from the claims in the previous case: either they are mutually causal, or they overlap. Among them, nuisance removal and return of land use right are mutually causal, while compensation for losses for the entire period and compensation for losses for a portion of the period are mutually inclusive.

From another perspective, looking at the arguments of both parties in this case: For appellee Dumiao Timber Market, if the previous judgment could be actually enforced, and the land use right in dispute returned to Dumiao Timber Market, it would not have filed this claim for "nuisance removal"; if the claim for compensation for losses in the previous case was enforced without discount, Dumiao Timber Market would definitely not again claim compensation for losses after January 1, 2015. For appellant Cong Jiagen, his defense arguments in both instances merely emphasize that not only should this case not support the claims of plaintiff Dumiao Timber Market, but also the effective judgment in the previous case was erroneous. In summary, the claims of Dumiao Timber Market in these two cases, no matter how you look at them, are overlapping and redundant.

The principle of res judicata in civil procedure law includes two aspects: First, a party shall not file a lawsuit again regarding a case already filed with the court; second, after a judgment takes effect, res judicata arises, and the parties shall not file another lawsuit regarding the legal relationship in dispute. From the court's perspective, it shall not accept such lawsuits, to avoid contradictory judgments and to avoid entanglement of the parties and resulting litigation fatigue. A judgment that is confirmed to be unenforceable, i.e., a judgment lacking enforceability, not only has a questionable outcome but is also likely to be improper or even completely erroneous. A judgment that encounters enforcement obstacles should not be simply artificially cut off at a certain point in time, with enforcement before and a separate lawsuit after. At the same time, if the dispute between the parties can be resolved within the enforcement procedure, then the effective judgment in the previous case need not initiate a trial supervision procedure; otherwise, the parties should be informed to resolve the issue by applying for retrial of the effective judgment in the previous case. That being the case, the only logical conclusion in this case is that the claim for return of land use right in the previous case and the claim for nuisance removal in this case are essentially the same "matter", and therefore, the court should rule to dismiss the claim in this case.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 124, item 5, Article 170, paragraph 1, item 2, and Article 175 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and Articles 247 and 330 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Huaibei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province rendered the following ruling on September 14, 2015:

1. Revoke the Civil Judgment (2015) Sui Min Yi Chu Zi No. 00206 of the Suixi County People's Court of Anhui Province;

2. Dismiss the lawsuit of appellee Suixi County Dumiao Timber Large Market Co., Ltd.

This ruling is final.
